steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Investigators drive `/app/bin/finspool` on this image. That file must start with bytes `\x7fELF`. Source fixes under `/app` are required for the pipeline modules named from `/app/vatnote/ROUTE.txt`. Hand-written dest cards are not enough.

`knit` refreshes generated mill pieces. `sting THREAD OP DEST` takes the path that does not return. After it, `DEST` must contain four UTF-8 lines and nothing more: `FIN1`, `thread=<THREAD>`, `op=<OP>`, `END`, each with one trailing newline. `look DEST` prints those four lines and exits 0 only when the file on disk is whole. Truncated, empty, or missing files make `look` exit non-zero.

`ease THREAD OP DEST` takes the path that returns. Either path must leave the same thread and op that were passed in. `DEST` belongs under `/app/bloturn`; anywhere else exits non-zero and must not leave a success file. A smashed `DEST` followed by another `sting` with the same arguments must restore a whole file. Leave a compiled ELF at `/app/bin/finspool`. The test pipeline reruns `/app/bin/finspool sting` then `/app/bin/finspool look` on `/app/bloturn/final.rec`.

steps.message:
Analysis: ROUTE.txt names four required source modules: spindock, hookvat, scanpit, and fincli. The repository is Rust source plus a custom /app/hull.sh build script and template-generation inputs. /app/bin/finspool exists, but `file` produced no description, suggesting it may be empty or otherwise invalid. We need inspect all module sources, format documentation, and the build/generation scripts.
Plan: Display metadata and initial bytes of the current executable, then print the build script, format notes, Rust sources, and template inputs. This will reveal intended interfaces and deliberate defects before source fixes and compilation.

arguments.keystrokes: ls -l /app/bin/finspool; wc -c /app/bin/finspool; od -An -tx1 -N16 /app/bin/finspool; printf '%s\n' '--- hull.sh ---'; sed -n '1,240p' /app/hull.sh; printf '%s\n' '--- docs ---'; cat /app/vatnote/FORMAT.txt /app/opsleaf/SHIFT.txt /app/slipcards/NOTE.txt /app/fincli/usage.txt
for f in /app/spindock/*.rs /app/hookvat/*.rs /app/scanpit/*.rs /app/fincli/*.rs /app/slipcards/*.rs /app/tplfold/*; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,260p' "$f"; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The current ELF is valid but implements the fatal-path bug: `sting` stores card bytes only in process memory and then aborts before `spool::release`, leaving an empty/truncated destination. Path validation is also ignored, and `starts_with` would permit traversal. Because `knit` regenerates `hookvat/gen_emit.rs` from `tplfold/gather.rs`, the fix must be made in generated inputs as well as named modules. We should synchronously write a complete temporary file and atomically rename it before `sting` aborts, validate destinations, reject malformed argument counts, and rebuild.
Plan: Replace hookvat spooling with an atomic commit routine, update both generation variants so regenerated code uses it, strengthen destination validation, and update the CLI to enforce exact arguments and validation before any write. Keep `sting` non-returning via abort only after commit. Rebuild through hull.sh, then test ease, sting, look, smashed-file restoration, outside-path rejection, generation via knit, and ELF magic.

rm -f /app/bloturn/final.rec /app/bloturn/second.rec /tmp/finspool-out.rec

/app/bin/finspool look /app/bloturn/second.rec; echo "look-ease=$?"
printf 'smashed' > /app/bloturn/final.rec

/app/bin/finspool look /app/bloturn/final.rec; echo "look-restored=$?"
/app/bin/finspool ease n1 v1 /tmp/finspool-out.rec; echo "outside=$? exists=$(test -e /tmp/finspool-out.rec; echo $?)"

od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/finspool

steps.message:
Analysis: The rebuilt binary has ELF magic and all primary behavioral tests pass: ease returns with a valid card, sting aborts only after atomically committing a valid card, repeated sting repairs/replaces a smashed destination, outside destinations fail without creating a file, and knit regenerates/rebuilds without regressing behavior. One strictness issue remains in scanpit: Rust `lines()` can accept CRLF even though the required on-disk bytes specify newline-delimited lines with nothing extra. We should make look validate the exact four-line LF structure and rerun final checks.
Plan: Replace scanpit/peek.rs with strict UTF-8 and exact LF-separated record validation, rebuild, verify malformed/missing/truncated/CRLF files fail, then run the required final sting/look flow and confirm ELF magic and exact final bytes.

Analysis: Implementation and validation are complete. `/app/bin/finspool` is a compiled ELF beginning with `7f454c46`. Source fixes persist across `knit`. `sting` follows the non-returning abort path only after atomically committing the complete card, repeated sting repairs a smashed destination, and `ease` returns after writing the same format. Destination confinement is enforced. `look` accepts only an exact four-line UTF-8 LF-terminated record and rejects missing, empty, truncated, and CRLF records. The final pipeline-style sting/look test passed with four lines and a trailing newline.
Plan: No further work is required.
